changeset-claim-re-read

## ⚠️ 2 pending changeset(s) describe a file this change touches

Their bodies publish **verbatim** into the CHANGELOG at the next release, so this is a request to **re-read them against your diff** — addressed here because you are the one seat that can answer it without re-deriving anything.

⛔ Nothing here blocks, and nothing here is a verdict on your change. This gate exits 0, is not a required context, and judges **name resolution, never meaning**: it asked whether a pending body names a file you touched. "Is this sentence still true?" is the one question it will not answer, and the one you are being asked to answer.

### `.changeset/7658-toc-code-span-anchor-parity.md`

- names `content/docs/utilities/cli.mdx` → `content/docs/utilities/cli.mdx` — edited by this change

  > Seven live headings in this repo's own docs were affected (`content/docs/utilities/cli.mdx`, `content/docs/utilities/runner.mdx`, `packages/cli/README.md`). Pinned against the real render pipeline rather than a second derivation of the slug rules: the new test renders each heading through `MarkdownImpl` and compares `extractToc`'s id to the `id` attribute `rehype-slug` actually emitted.

- names `packages/cli/README.md` → `packages/cli/README.md` — edited by this change

Pinned against the real render pipeline rather than a second derivation of the slug rules: the new test renders each heading through `MarkdownImpl` and compares `extractToc`'s id to the `id` attribute `rehype-slug` actually emitted.

### `.changeset/7694-chart-series-chart-type-alias-refusal.md`

- names `packages/cli/src/cli.ts` → `packages/cli/src/cli.ts` — edited by this change

  > - **Before:** `series: [{ name: 'revenue', chartType: 'line' }]` validated green through `@object-ui/types/zod` (`safeValidateSchema`, `objectui check` / `objectui validate`, any pipeline that keeps `parse()`'s output) — and the key was gone from the output, so a consumer of the parse result drew that series in the chart's own family, precisely what the author was overriding. On the TypeScript face the key was merely an excess property on a fresh literal; a widened object carrying it assigned structurally. - **After:** the same document REFUSES at `series[i].chartType` (issue code `invalid_type`) with one message on both channels — the parse-time issue and the `.describe()` metadata: `Unrecognized key(s) on this chart series: \`chartType\`. Did you mean \`chartType\` → \`type\`? …` followed by the reason and the remedy. Write `type: 'bar' | 'line' | 'area'`. On the TypeScript face `ChartDataSeries.chartType` is a `?: never` tombstone, so both the fresh literal and the widened assignment are `tsc` errors. - **Both written** (`{ type: 'bar', chartType: 'line' }`) is refused at `chartType` alone — the key is not folded onto `type` and no precedence is minted between the two spellings. - **Which documents to scan.** The narrowing does not stop at `ChartDataSeriesSchema`; it reaches every document through the parents that embed it — `ChartSchema.series` (`zod/data-display.zod.ts`, `z.array(ChartDataSeriesSchema)`) and, one level further out, `ReportSectionSchema.chart` (`zod/reports.zod.ts`, `ChartSchema.optional()`). Authors meet it through `safeValidateSchema()` (`zod/index.zod.ts`, which parses `AnyComponentSchema`) and through the CLI's `objectui validate` command (`packages/cli/src/cli.ts`). In practice: every `chart` node's `series[]`, and every report section whose `chart` carries one.

Read the **paragraph**, not the line: both false halves of the objectui#8617 claim sat in one paragraph, and correcting either alone would have left it asserting the same wrong thing.

If a claim did go false, **correct the body**. That is precedented and prose-only, frontmatter untouched; `check-changeset-overwrite.mjs` will report the correction as its own case 2 ("correcting a declaration on purpose … legitimate"), which is the intended shape — one gate asks for the read, the other records the write.

Not covered, stated so nobody reads this as more: a born-false claim that spells no line address at all (objectui#9495 coordinated one by ORDINAL — "a grep finds that member first" — and deciding that means reading what the sentence means), a claim spelled as a symbol or a package rather than a backticked file name, and a file named ambiguously.

Compared the checked-out tree with `1fe05ff37` (merge-base with origin/main): 6 file(s) changed outside `.changeset/`, read against 2042 pending declaration(s) that publish a body (2671 pending in total). · [run](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/actions/runs/37050922613)

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `5e7b894313cb899540946edcb9cea832b4f27421`
Local-runs: none
Rendered: 2026-10-02T19:17Z

PR objectui#11499 (card objectui#11496), judged against triage's ruling `5958245941` ("Ruling: retire", with the family close-out over every command and flag `cli.ts` declares), on the precedents PR objectui#11487 (record `5957439389`) and PR objectui#11495 (record `5958276867`). Read for this record: the card body and all four comments on it; the PR body with its close-out table, and its 7-file list; the net diff of the head against `main` (merge-base `1fe05ff37`..head, +141 / −107 over `.changeset/11496-retire-cli-add.md`, `content/docs/utilities/cli.mdx`, `packages/cli/README.md`, `packages/cli/src/__tests__/cli-bin.test.ts`, `packages/cli/src/cli.ts`, `packages/cli/src/commands/add.ts` deleted, `packages/cli/src/commands/analyze.ts`; `main` has since moved one commit to `b654d4ed5`, PR objectui#11497, whose diff over `packages/cli`, `cli.mdx` and `.changeset/` adds one unrelated changeset and nothing else, and the three-dot diff against current `main` is byte-identical to the merge-base diff); and the check-runs on the head, polled at one-minute intervals until every run had completed. Nothing was built, run or re-run locally: the head's tree is read with `git show` / `git grep` against the fetched ref, the dev's reverse-verification legs are read as reported, and the head's own check-runs are the gate verdicts. Placeholders are spelled in capitals (`COMPONENT`, `TYPE NAME`) because the body sanitizer strips angle-bracket shapes.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **The published bin's accept set narrows by one command — right.** `cli.ts` at the head declares no `add`; the import of `./commands/add.js` is gone and the file is deleted. `packages/cli/src` sets no `allowUnknownOption`, `passThroughOptions`, `allowExcessArguments`, `enablePositionalOptions` or `exitOverride` (grep at the head: none), and the CLI runs commander `^15`, whose default refuses an undeclared command with `error: unknown command 'add'` and a non-zero exit before any action runs. So the retirement is a refusal, not a silent accept, and nothing is written. No bespoke refusal branch was needed and none was added, which is the ruling's "no placeholder kept".
2. **...and by two options — right.** `analyze` declares no `.option(` at the head; commander's default refuses `--render-performance` and `--bundle-size` as unknown options. The one measured no-op (`--render-performance`: fixed text, byte-identical in an empty directory and in a built project, exit 0) is retired under the ruling's close-out clause, "any other no-op found is retired in the same PR".
3. **`--bundle-size` goes with it — right** (the dev's open question 1, option A). Before, the flag chose between the bundle report and the render section; with the render section retired it would select between nothing and be read by no code, which is exactly the shape ruling `5955124315` retired `generate --output` for. It is a no-op the same PR creates, so the close-out clause covers it. No producer of the spelling exists at the head (`git grep` for `--bundle-size` finds only the changeset, the pins and unrelated prose about size budgets). The seat answered A; this record concurs.
4. **Nothing stands in for any of the three — right.** `add.ts` is deleted, not stubbed; `analyze.ts` loses `AnalyzeOptions`, `analyzeRenderPerformance` and the `runAll` selector, and `analyze()` now runs `analyzeBundleSize()` and nothing else. The no-flag report is the old report minus the render section, which is what the control pin asserts.
5. **The root `--help` narrows, and the enumeration pin reads both directions — right.** `cli.ts` at the head carries 14 `.command(` declarations (`serve dev build start init lint test generate doctor studio check validate create analyze`), and `SUBCOMMANDS` in `cli-bin.test.ts` is those 14. `helpCommandNames` parses the `Commands:` section (an entry starts with exactly two spaces, a wrapped description line does not, `generate|g` reads as `generate`), the lit control reads commander's own `help` as the last entry, and the assertions are set equality plus no duplicates. It replaces a `toContain` loop that a retired command coming back would have passed. This is the ruling's "one enumeration pin over the built CLI's commands".
6. **The docs surface narrows — right where the diff reaches, and one published file beyond the diff is left stale.** In `cli.mdx` the `add` section goes, the `analyze` flag table becomes one paragraph that matches `analyze.ts` at the head (total, JavaScript and CSS sizes of `dist/` under the current directory, the ten largest files; `objectui build` does default to `dist`, `cli.ts:80` and `commands/build.ts:26`), and the stored count "The CLI exposes 15 commands" becomes a pointer to `objectui --help`, so it cannot go stale again. The heading list at `main` and at the head differs only by the removed `add` heading. `packages/cli/README.md` loses its `add` section; its combined `check / doctor / studio / analyze / create plugin` heading names no flag and needs no change. **But** `skills/objectui/guides/project-setup.md`, unchanged from `main`, still carries in its "CLI commands" table row 174, `objectui add` — "Add a component renderer scaffold", and row 177, `objectui analyze` — "Analyze bundle size / render performance". After this diff the first prescribes a command the bin refuses and the second claims a capability the bin no longer has. The file is in the published skills catalog, outside the ruling's named surfaces and outside the claim's file surface, and neither the dev report, the PR body nor the seat's ACCEPT names it. Judged: the diff is right, and the `add` reader sweep was not run beyond `packages/cli` and `content/docs`; carried to ③ with its remedy. Every other `objectui add` hit at the head is a literal slug fixture (`toc-anchor-parity.test.tsx` `LIVE_SHAPES`, the `check-doc-links` test and comment) or the 7658 changeset's past-tense account, none a prescription to run the command.
7. **Where `analyze` reads is unchanged — right.** `dist/` under the current directory, the "Bundle Size Analysis" banner and paths relative to `dist/` (`assets/probe-bundle.js`) are what the control pin asserts. The command's help description, "Analyze application performance", and its first printed line, "ObjectUI Performance Analyzer", are untouched and now read wider than the bundle report that is all it does — a wording residue of the `doctor` kind the PR already lists in Acceptance notes, not an accept-set change; named for the next toucher, not blocking.
8. **No programmatic export moves — right.** `@object-ui/cli`'s `exports` is `./dist/index.js`, which re-exports `serve` and `init` only; `cli.ts` is the `bin` entry and `tsup` builds `cli` and `index` as separate entries. `package.json` is not in the diff. The "no exported symbol moves" sentence in the PR body and the changeset holds.
9. **The family close-out — right in shape and coverage.** The PR body's 22 rows cover every `.command(` and every `.option(` `cli.ts` declares at the head, plus `-V` / `-h` and commander's `help`, each with the help text, the docs text and the measured built-CLI behaviour. Partials are named, not implemented; `validate` and `check` are left to draft PR objectui#11069 as the claim required; the three class (a) failures (`create plugin`, `lint` / `test`, `studio`) are carried by objectui#11500 (open, created 2026-10-02T19:04Z).
10. **The pins pin the ruling, through the built bin — right.** The `add` refusal (exit non-zero, stderr matches `unknown command 'add'`, the directory stays empty) carries a same-directory write control (`g page Probe` then exits 0 and writes exactly `pages`, `pages/probe.json`), so an empty tree cannot be a read-only directory. The `analyze` refusals are an `it.each` over both flags with the same three assertions; the control plants `dist/assets/probe-bundle.js` and asserts exit 0, the banner, the file and no render section; the help pin's lit control is `analyze`'s own usage line. All spawn `dist/cli.js`, where the card measured the defect. `readdirSync` with `recursive: true` needs Node 20 or later; `engines` pins 22.11 or later. The `Array.at` call was replaced by an index read because the package's `tsconfig` `lib` is `ES2020` (judged by `Type Check`, tally below). The dev's reverse verification is read, not re-run: BASE 6 failed / 41 passed on the six predicted names; the ablation planted an exit-0 `add` and both option lines back into the committed `cli.ts` and failed the predicted five (the no-flag control stays green because `analyze.ts` was not mutated); restored, 47 passed. The diff's own index lines (`ab22eb7e6..004165f17` for `cli.ts`, `7d9e7e3af..63659c0b3` for `analyze.ts`, `b2fd2fcae` for the deleted `add.ts`) name the same blobs the dev reports. `cli-bin.test.ts` is a `*.test.ts` file, not in the `dist` project, so the pins are judged by the eight `Test (shard N/8)` runs.
11. **Serial and base — right.** The merge-base `1fe05ff37` IS the landing commit of PR objectui#11495, the ruling's named serial constraint, so this diff sits on top of the `--from` retirement rather than beside it. `main` has moved one commit (PR objectui#11497), which adds `.changeset/11479-producers-declared-types.md` and touches nothing under `packages/cli`, `cli.mdx` or the README, so not merging `main` was right and the queue's rebuild carries no risk from this diff.
12. **Repository surface — right.** Three commits, each with the model-free trailer pair AGENTS.md prescribes; no model identifier in the PR title, body, changeset or commits. `Governed Surface Queue Guard` is green: the 7 paths are not a governed surface.
